data.title: RUNE up 15% after hackers use THORChain to launder stolen funds — What next?
data.description:
THORChain’s native token RUNE rallied by over 15% in the last 24 hours as the broader market lost $160 billion in capitalization. The decline followed Binance’s hack, which saw the centralized exchange (CEX) lose around $6.30 billion.

Hence, the question: Why is the token’s performance independent of the general market right now?

Is THORChain abetting laundering of funds from crypto hacks?

Hackers have regularly used THORChain to launder funds stolen from the crypto market.

For instance, funds from the Binance hack were commingled to a similar address that received $388 million from the Bitget incident after arriving via THORChain. This evidence might be a suggestion that the same actor is likely responsible.

The pattern has been evident from the swap volumes and fees on the chain, which have increased significantly. Fees hit a weekly high of $11K, confirming a spike in network activity.

Swap volumes showed that a total of $62.08 million went through the mainnet, while $94 million was processed through its bridges in other wallets.

As far as the hack is concerned, $8.94 million was converted to Bitcoin [BTC], and Ethereum [ETH] accounted for $6.17 million, while other tokens were swapped for $1.18 million.

As a result of a spike in network activity, the daily trading volume of RUNE surged by over 393%.

However, users are still worried that the chain could be abetting the laundering of funds. This, because other chains like Arbitrum One [ARB] froze the funds, but THORChain did not. In fact, immediately after the incident, THORChain posted,

Digital money needs digital freedom.

While they did not support the hack directly, the language used combined with the timing of the post raised many concerns. One user on X mocked the post, commenting,

Free to hack.

RUNE faces resistance at $0.70 despite strong buying

On the price charts, RUNE rose aggressively from $0.58 to $0.723, but it could not stay above $0.70 for long. The brief dip below $0.60 came immediately after the hack incident, but the altcoin reclaimed it as the floor.

The $0.70-level has been a resistance for the past month, but the strong buying pressure failed at this zone.

Moreover, the MACD bars turned green and grew bigger, asserting the buying pressure. The Chaikin Money Flow (CMF) reinforced capital inflows into the chain, rising from -0.04 to 0.31.

Therefore, RUNE will remain in a bearish structure on the 4-hour chart unless $0.70 is turned into support. Otherwise, the altcoin could continue bouncing between $0.60 and $0.70, but there is a chance it could break down.

Final Summary

  • RUNE surged by over 15% as hackers moved stolen funds via THORChain, leading to high network activity. 
  • RUNE bulls are facing resistance at $0.70 despite strong buying pressure, suggesting that the rally could be short-lived.

data.title: PYTH crypto sees $179M drop in secured value – Can prices recover?
data.description:
Pyth Network [PYTH] has recorded a massive decline over the past day, with the asset plummeting roughly 12% to a new local low at press time.

The reaction, expectedly, followed the Binance hack incident, which reportedly resulted in losses of roughly $6.3 billion. However, a closer look shows that the protocol has also recorded one of its weakest-performing months.

Perpetual market activity has further fueled the decline, as traders concentrate capital on shorting PYTH.

PYTH records a $179M capital outflow

The decline in PYTH was accompanied by a massive on-chain capital outflow, tracked through Total Value Secured (TVS).

TVS tracks the total value of assets managed by the protocol, including bridged and native tokens. The decline suggests that market participants are pulling back from active utility. Over the past day, TVS dropped from $3.164 billion to $2.985 billion, marking an outflow of $179 million in the past 24 hours as of writing .

More concerning is that Pyth Network’s earnings have also plummeted significantly over the past day, according to data from DeFiLlama. Earnings, which track gross profit after incentives, have fallen to roughly $1,310 at press time, the lowest level ever recorded on a monthly basis.

In fact, this represents a significant decline from September, when the protocol earned $434,640. When earnings drop to this level, it points to reduced protocol utility as users become more reluctant to engage with the platform.

Perpetual traders increase short positions

Sellers have dominated perpetual trading activity as they continue to expand their positions.

Funding Rate data for PYTH‘s perpetual market shows a significant concentration of short positions, with the rate falling to -0.0172 as of writing.

PYTH’s negative Funding Rate, now at an extreme level, shows that traders have positioned roughly $36.77 million in the perpetual market towards shorting the asset.

When broken down by trader category, the data shows that whales, traders who control large amounts of capital in the market, have been key participants influencing price dynamics.

The Whale-Retail Delta, which tracks the difference between whale and retail trading activity, rose to 0.301 over the past day as whale positioning in the asset continued to increase.

Spot traders accumulate despite the decline

Spot traders, despite the negative outlook, have been accumulating the asset.

According to CoinGlass, Spot Netflow tracks the inflow and outflow of capital on exchanges. When outflows exceed inflows, it suggests that more assets are being withdrawn from exchanges, potentially indicating accumulation.

Netflow currently stands at -$1.56 million, suggesting that following the decline, more capital has moved out of exchanges than into them. This outlook may stem from investors viewing the recent drop as a discount.

data.title: Ethereum wallet permission used in Binance attack, Blockaid says
data.description:
Security firm Blockaid says an attacker used Ethereum’s EIP-7702 wallet feature to connect a Binance account to code capable of draining its assets. Its findings offer a closer look at the transfers flagged during the exchange’s October 29 security incident.

Key to the analysis are the wallet permissions. According to Blockaid, after a total of 50 different variations were submitted in a single transaction by the attacker, one permission kicked in, and the dangerous code got a route to grab money out of the account.

How the permission took effect

Through EIP-7702, an Ethereum account can delegate the execution of functions to a smart contract. Permissions are granted to the smart contract code, which determines permitted operations.

Blockaid noted that the said account had delegated to another contract with functions to withdraw tokens and Ether, with a specific “operator” address being authorized to access these operations.

Basically, the arrangement gave that operator a way to collect assets from the affected wallet, and even new funds that arrive in the account are not safe.

Fifty variations, one accepted

Blockaid also followed up and explained that the attacker apparently lacked the wallet’s current account counter.

That counter, called a nonce, helps to determine whether an authorization can be accepted. An actively used wallet’s counter changes as transactions are processed.

According to Blockaid, the attacker submitted 50 signed authorizations covering consecutive counter values. One matched the account’s counter when the transaction was included on the blockchain.

The firm summarized the result:

Only 1 of 50 was a hit.

Binance’s investigation continues

In its security update on October 30, Binance says the estimate of the incident’s total impact is about $6.3 billion. It said about $3 billion in affected assets had been frozen.

The exchange’s initial investigation pointed to a potentially compromised engineer’s laptop that allowed unauthorized withdrawals. Binance has said it would cover losses.

Binance has promised a technical report after completing its investigation.

Final Summary

  • Blockaid says an EIP-7702 authorization connected a Binance wallet to asset-draining code.
  • It has not been mentioned how the attacker was able to get the required signatures.

data.title: ‘Our collateral resides off-exchange’ – Ethena downplays $8.8M Binance exposure
data.description:
Ethena, the protocol behind the synthetic, yield-generating stablecoin USDe, has downplayed exposure to the Binance hack. The team clarified that all their USDe backing resides offchain with its custodians, not on centralized exchanges. 

In fact, for the Binance scenario, the team claimed only $8.8 million in unrealized PnL (profit and loss) exposure to the platform. 

The total unrealized PNL exposure to Binance is ~$8.8M, far below the excess reserve fund of >$60m.

In a separate update following the FUD tied to the Binance exploit, Ethena added that independent attestors, Chainlink and Llama Risk, have verified its overcollateralized backing for USDe. 

Each of these independent 3rd parties mentioned above have confirmed USDe remains overcollateralised by more than $60m at >101.0%.

But before evaluating the claims, AMBCrypto explored why the community seemed worried about Ethena’s outsized exposure to the exploit. 

Ethena’s massive partnership with Binance

Ethena and Binance recently signed a partnership agreement for RWA (real-world assets) basis trade. This involves Binance’s bStocks, which promised an 11% yield and a great expansion into a $150T opportunity in the equity sector for USDe backing. 

The deal was signed last month, but the exposure seems relatively small. 

According to Ethena, RWA basis accounts for $51 million, or 1.2% of its $4.54 billion collateral for USDe. Beyond the RWA basis, Ethena also uses the crypto basis across Bitcoin [BTC] and Ethereum [ETH] to hunt for yield. The crypto basis segment accounts for about 17% of the USDe backing ($628 million) and is spread across Binance, Deribit, Coinbase, Huobi, Bybit, OKX, and Hyperliquid. 

Collectively, this is about 18% USDe collateral exposure to crypto platforms for RWA and crypto basis. In fact, the largest share of the collateral is DeFi lending ($1.3 billion) across Aave and Morpho. But Aave was also affected and paused operations after the Binance hack. So, the contagion risk fears over Ethena’s exposure to the exploit were warranted. 

However, as the project mentioned, it has off-exchange settlements (OES) or custody arrangements with Coinbase, Copper, and Ceffu. So, the risk may be limited, as the project said. 

In fact, Mikhail Kedzel, Founder of Yumi Finance, confirmed that Binance offers such off-chain arrangements to top institutional players. 

For everyone asking why: it’s because Ethena doesn’t keep funds in Binance’s hot wallet. They keep it with their custodian, and Binance just ‘recognizes’ it as funds stored at the CEX. Stuff only really available to the big guys.

It’s like the ‘custodied collateral lending’ design being explored by Aave. 

That said, the Binance attacker stole and dumped 217 million ENA ($34 million) for ETH. This dragged ENA below $0.19 after a 16% drop. Whether Ethena’s clarification on the Binance hack is enough to stop the pullback remains unclear. 

Final Summary

  • Ethena clarified that it can cover the $8.8 million Binance exposure.
  • Binance attacker sold $33 million in ENA for ETH to avoid seizure and freezing.

data.title: How did Binance hacker leverage Aave to outsmart Tether, Circle freeze?
data.description:
The Binance hacker pre-empted some of the industry’s potential reactions and planned countermeasures, including using Aave and UniswapX to avoid seizures and fund freezes. 

On Thursday, the attacker, now confirmed as North Korea’s TraderTraitor, made an initial $3.79B sweep on the Ethereum network, including 200,630 ETH and some stablecoins. 

Knowing that Tether, Circle, and other platforms would move quickly to freeze the stablecoins and other assets, the attacker deposited $60M USDT on Aave and borrowed out 19,760 WETH ($45.13M). This happened between 20:58 UTC and 21:01 UTC on Thursday, 29th October.  

Similarly, TraderTraitor swapped $325M USDT using UniswapX and Iinch between 21:34 UTC and 21:09 UTC.

In fact, analysts noticed that the hacker was forced to pay 10% of their swapped amount to fast-track the orders before freezing began. The UniswapX transfers took about 35 minutes, while Aave borrowing took only 5 minutes. Subsequently, the hacker unwrapped the WETH and got the native, unfreezable 142,062 ETH.  

Tether and Circle began the freezes by around 21:18 UTC, stopping further conversions. However, the attacker now had 420K ETH (unwrapped 142K ETH, original 200K ETH from Binance wallets, and other swapped non-USDT assets). 

Commenting on the unfortunate but massive scheme, one analyst said, 

The Binance hacker might have just pulled off one of the smartest moves I’ve seen in crypto. Tether can freeze the USDT sitting in the wallet. But it can’t freeze the ETH he already borrowed.

He added, 

So now Aave is left holding frozen collateral, while the hacker is sitting on liquid ETH.

Aave denies bad debt claims after Binance hack

Here, it’s worth noting that the KelpDAO hack leveraged a similar DeFi lending loophole to cash out and launder stolen funds. Aave was left with over $120M in bad debt. 

However, Aave founder Stani Kulechov denied that bad debt claims were applicable to the Binance hack incident. 

Actually, there is no bad debt, in fact, it’s over-collateralized with stable collateral. Kelp was different.

What remains unclear, however, is who will be repaid the $60M: Is it Binance, the primary victim, or Aave, which is also a secondary victim? 

In fact, some have even wondered how over $1M was allowed to be signed off without human review, let alone $325M swept from some of Binance’s hot wallets. For centralized exchanges such as Binance, caps make sense. However, for non-custodial decentralized platforms, it’s a different setup that is designed to have no human intervention. 

According to Chainalysis, platforms running the wallets on Ethereum with the bug that the attacker used should now be vigilant and upgrade accordingly. 

Final Summary

  • Binance hacker used Aave and UniswapX to swap $365M USDT to unfreezable +120K ETH.
  • Aave denied claims that the incident left it with bad debt like the KelpDAO exploit.

data.title: Why Celestia crypto’s breakdown below $0.47 could trigger more TIA losses
data.description:
Celestia [TIA] plunged 14.03% in 24 hours at press time, as fresh macroeconomic uncertainty triggered heavy selling across the altcoin market, deepening its recent losses.

This steep decline accompanied the Federal Reserve’s hawkish stance and persistent inflation concerns, which weakened demand for riskier altcoins.

Particularly, the Federal Reserve preserved its cautious monetary policy stance on the 28th of October. Additionally, September’s PCE inflation matched expectations at 3.6% annually, validating concerns about extended restrictive interest rates.

Despite the price decline, the token’s trading volume interestingly surged 38.04% to $72.72 million.

This divergence implied an elevated trading activity during the sell-off, even though the volume increase could not solely establish sellers’ dominance.

TIA traders retreat as Open Interest collapses

Celestia’s derivatives market registered a considerable contraction in trader exposure, beyond the spot market decline.

According to CoinGlass, TIA’s Open Interest (OI) dropped 28.60% to $75.86 million, suggesting that traders closed positions as the token’s price continued falling. The shrinking OI alone, however, could not distinguish voluntary position closures from forced liquidations.

Therefore, for Celestia, the depreciation emerged in the midst of a broader retreat in the speculative participation. As the derivatives positions diminished, the market encountered reduced leveraged exposure despite the increased trading activity.

Spot and Futures sellers tighten their grip

The bearish pressure notably extended across Celestia‘s spot and derivatives markets, confirming the weakness evident in its price performance.

As CryptoQuant analytics, TIA’s Spot Taker Cumulative Volume Delta (CVD) highlighted taker-sell dominance, implying aggressive sellers outweighed buyers executing market orders. Additionally, the Futures Taker CVD also showed taker-sell dominance, revealing similar behavior among the derivatives investors.

These readings together pointed towards a coordinated bearish pressure across the two markets. Noteworthy, unlike the falling OI, which implied declining outstanding positions, the CVD indicator highlighted the direction of aggressive trading.

The persistent selling across both markets therefore complicated TIA’s recovery attempts, and without a stronger buying participation, the token could struggle to reverse its recent losses.

TIA loses crucial support as bears advance

On the daily timeframe chart, Celestia’s price structure strengthened the bearish outlook after the token broke below the $0.4727 support level.

Notably, the price breakdown emerged after an earlier rejection around the $0.5548 zone, which had already weakened the token’s recovery structure.

The Parabolic SAR indicator, meanwhile, remained above the price at around $0.6616 as of press time, preserving its bearish signal.

Additionally, further weakness emerged from the RSI indicator, which fell to 39.44, remaining below its moving average, and suggesting deteriorating buying strength.

Consequently, the breakdown exposed the $0.3277 level as the next major support, even though buyers still had a better chance of intervening before that level.

A decisive reclaim of the $0.4727 resistance, however, could ease immediate selling pressure and reopen a recovery attempt toward the $0.5548 region.

Final Summary

  • Celestia plunged 14% as selling intensified and traders reduced their derivatives exposure.
  • TIA’s breakdown below $0.4727 raised the risk of further losses toward $0.3277.

data.title: Top 8 Solana APIs of October 2026
data.description:
Solana APIs are applications, websites, or bots that interact with the Solana blockchain. APIs essentially act as a messenger between software, letting applications ask for data or carry out a process. They are useful and help apps, services, or platforms work together across various systems.

APIs on Solana can help to retrieve wallet information and check SOL balances, token holdings and fetch transaction data and retrieve transaction history, and other details. Users can also access NFT data, ownership information, and digital asset details. Here are the top 8 Solana APIs for the month:

1. QuickNode

QuickNode provides a low-latency infrastructure and is built to scale dApps on the Solana blockchain. Developers can read blockchain data, submit transactions, interact with smart contracts, and build apps that need scalable blockchain connectivity.

It also aggregates traditional node infrastructure with advanced data products and transaction tools. Quicknode is great for developers who are building multi-chain dApps, NFT apps, DeFi platforms, and other enterprise blockchain solutions.

2. Helius

Helius offers a range of high-performance tools designed for speed and low latency, and gives users a chance to build Web3 applications and monitor transactions. It has a very user-friendly interface and simplifies complex blockchain interactions for its users.

The API has enhanced Solana RPC APIs and the Digital Asset Standard (DAS) API for NFT and token data. There is an option for real-time transaction and account monitoring along with webhooks for blockchain event notifications.

3. Alchemy 

Alchemy offers both access to real-time data and Solana infrastructure from the same provider, along with JSON-RPC and WebSocket connections. It also has Yellowstone gRPC for streaming live blockchain data and FAS and Photon APIs for tokens, NFTs, and compressed assets.

Solana Mainnet and Devnet are also supported, along with 99.99% reliability for its RPC and streaming API, multi-region infrastructure, and automatic failover to keep the connection running. Alchemy is used for wallets, DeFi apps, trading bots, custom indexers, and analytics platforms that need reliable RPC access as well as live Solana data.

4. Chainstack 

Chainstack is a node provider designed for teams looking for reliable blockchain access without having to run or build their own infrastructure. Both shared and dedicated nodes along with geo-distributed infrastructure for lower-latency access. More than 70 blockchains are supported on Chainstack, and a great option for team building applications across multiple networks.

There is a free tier for development and testing, while the paid plans scale based on factors such as throughput and node type rather than credits per API call. There is a 99.99% uptime and unlimited nodes for larger production workloads with stricter performance requirements.

5. ChangeNOW

ChangeNOW is different from other APIs as it focuses on crypto swaps more than on Solana data or node access. Wallets, dApps, exchanges, and payment platforms add in-app swaps without having to build their own exchange logic, liquidity routing, or transaction processing.

It supports 1,500 assets across 110+ blockchains with over 2.25 million exchange pairs and liquidity sourced from both centralized and decentralized exchanges. There are reports of 99.99% availability and a 350-millisecond response time.

6. CoinAPI 

CoinAPI focuses on crypto market data rather than direct access to the Solana network. Users can get data from 300 exchanges through a single API, giving developers access to real-time and historical SOL trades, quotes, order books, and OHLCV data.

There is also pay-as-you-go access with $25 in free monthly credits, and fixed plans start at $79 per month for Startup, followed by $249 for Streamer and $599 for Pro. Paid plans also include a 99.9% uptime SLA, while latency guarantees are available through custom Enterprise plans.

7. Moralis

Moralis supports EVM chains and Solana, and the API focuses on making blockchain data accessible through simple REST endpoints. It also focuses on token data, pricing, and NFT metadata, and gives a higher-level abstraction than raw RPC.

Users also get instant access to cross-chain blockchain data and allows users to pull normalized DeFi positions across major protocols via single API calls.

8. CoinStats

CoinStats gives developers actionable information instead of making them work with raw transaction data on Solana. It covers data from more than 120 blockchains and 10,000+ DeFi protocols that can be useful for wallets, tax tools, portfolio trackers, and dashboards that need to work across multiple networks.

There is also a credit-based pricing model, with requests using 30-50 credits depending on the endpoint. The free plan includes 50,000 monthly credits and up to 5 requests per second, while the paid plans start at $49 per month for 1 million credits.

Final word

Solana has a growing developer ecosystem which creates demand for reliable APIs that simplify blockchain connectivity and data access. APIs help developers build apps that can read data from and interact with and send transactions to the Solana blockchain.

User discretion is advised, and users should do their own research before investing.

data.title: Analyzing BNB’s rebound opportunities hours after $6.3B hack, altcoin sell-offs
data.description:
Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange by volume, reported a security breach incident with an estimated total impact of $6.3 billion. At the time of writing, roughly $3 billion of the affected assets had been frozen on-chain.

The incident caused panic in the markets and led to a Bitcoin [BTC] sell-off. In the 12 hours before press time, BTC’s price fell by 5.2% from $81.7K to $77.4K. Crypto liquidations measured $1.50 billion in the last 24 hours, with $1.28 billion in longs liquidated.

Binance Coin [BNB], the exchange token, fell by a commensurate 5.2% over the same time period. Co-founder and former CEO of Binance, Changpeng Zhao, assured users that funds were safe, pointing to Chief Customer Service Officer Yi He’s statement on X and the rapid response from Tether and Circle to freeze the affected assets.

Popular crypto analyst and trader Ali Martinez suggested that a buying opportunity could be around the corner. The $73K-level for BTC, Ethereum [ETH] at $2,000, and XRP at $1 would be his buy-the-dip targets.

Where would BNB offer such a similar opportunity?

On the 1-day chart, the swing structure flipped bearishly with a daily session close below $703.6. This level was the latest swing low in BNB’s uptrend from under $600 in August.

The price bounce from $680 to $718 at the time of writing brought the altcoin back into the Value Area, highlighted within the Fixed Range Volume Profile tool.

Plotted from the previous swing low, this tool marked the Value Area High (VAH) at $711 and VAL at $770, and the Point of Control at $750.

Traders’ call to action – Buy!

The latest bounce has brought BNB back within the short-term range from mid-September. However, the daily structure saw a bearish change of character. Hence, despite the bounce, swing traders need to be cautious.

BNB seemed to be presenting a risky buying opportunity. A deviation below the local range on the back of an unforseen news event like Binance’s hack, followed by a swift recovery, may be a possibility.

Whether this bullish scenario comes true depends on capital inflows that will be dictated by Bitcoin and the wider market’s sentiment.

Final Summary

  • Binance’s security incident has severely shaken market sentiment and led to a crypto market liquidation cascade.
  • BNB saw a sizeable retracement below its Value Area and will need to reclaim $700 with strong demand to keep the bullish bias alive.

data.title: QNT crypto’s price now down 50.5% from September’s high — Should you buy now?
data.description:
Quant [QNT] has shed 50.5% of its value from the $373-high it made on 27th September. The most recent losses saw QNT crypto’s price fall below the psychological $200-support.

News of the Binance hack to the tune of an estimated $6.3 billion, the largest in history, has also driven markets into a selling frenzy. In fact, Bitcoin [BTC] slipped below the $80k round-number level too, spurring altcoin losses.

In this environment of steady selling and a month-long retracement, Quant might be offering a high-risk short-term buying opportunity. Swing investors might want to wait a bit longer for a momentum shift confirmation before looking to re-enter.

Sizeable September rally keeps current structure firmly bullish

The swing structure on the daily chart was bearish, captured by the Fibonacci retracement levels (orange). At the time of writing, the 61.8% retracement level at $178.8 was being respected as support.

Even so, the internal structure was bearish, as evidenced by the price dip below $223.5 earlier this month to form a new local low at $173.56.

In the coming days, a daily session close below $173.5 would be a sign that QNT’s price was heading towards the 78.6% retracement level at $126.

Traders should remember that sentiment remains fragile following the Binance hack news.

QNT’s price bounce expected due to H4 shift

The 4-hour chart seemed to be more encouraging though. The bullish structure shift made earlier this week, when the price broke above the $212.87-swing level, was still intact. The subsequent retracement back towards $180 might be ending.

The technical indicators did not yet show a reversal. The OBV was balanced between buying and selling pressure, and the RSI moved below neutral 50.

Based on the price action, buying QNT at these prices could be feasible. The bullish target would be $223.5, while invalidation lay below $173.56.

As the daily chart showed, a drop below $173.5 could see a QNT price slide all the way down to $126.

Final Summary

  • The Clearing House partnership and cascading long squeezes fueled QNT’s bull trend.
  • A price drop below $173.5 would signal QNT price weakness, but for now, the narrative could regain strength if the wider market begins to recover.

data.title: 10% to 56%: USDC’s remarkable rise in euro-paired stablecoin trading
data.description:
Since December 2023, USD Coin [USDC] has increased its market share of euro-paired stablecoin trade from 10% to 56% as of October.

While at the end of 2024, euro-paired stablecoin trade volume reached levels near $10 billion per month before declining in subsequent months.

As a result of MiCA restrictions on Tether [USDT], the number of transactions using USDC increased. This gave USDC an advantage as it pushed more trading activity toward USDC.

Julia Kovalchuk, Head of B2B Product at Paybis, a MiCA-licensed crypto and fiat infrastructure provider, told AMBCrypto in an exclusive interview, 

After MiCA, USDC grew from about 21% to 75% of stablecoin volume among our payment-firm clients in a year. The US leans toward USDC too, while USDT still dominates trading and emerging markets. Winners are regional and split by use case – USDC is the default choice for enterprise payment companies, traditional-finance on-ramps, and regulated custody in both the EU and the US.

Specifically, since Tether had been denied access to euro markets, euro-paired USDC order books now have 40% more depth than those of USDT/EUR order books.

Therefore, larger euro-paired stablecoin trades were able to be executed without causing as much price movement.

This gives USDC an advantage for traders converting euros into dollar-backed stablecoins. Nevertheless, the global supply of USDT is 2.5 times larger than that of USDC.

The 56% level of euro-paired trading of USDC, however, indicates how regulation may be able to move trading activity and liquid assets from one stablecoin to another.

MiCA rules give USDC an edge over USDT in Europe

The shift in market leadership demonstrates a much broader trend of changes occurring in the European regulatory environment.

MiCA established a July 2026 deadline for all stablecoin issuers to obtain EU authorization and demonstrate they comply with reserve and supervision requirements.

Still, Tether’s USDT remains unauthorized. However, Circle received authorization via a French electronic-money license. In response to the regulations, Coinbase began restricting USDT trading for its European customers.

AMBCrypto asked Kovalchuk what compliance means in a world governed by MiCA-style regulations. She responded,

In Europe, liquidity is easy to find. A license takes years and costly legal work, so many smaller firms plug into licensed infrastructure like ours. The US GENIUS Act, Hong Kong’s Stablecoins Ordinance, and the UAE’s payment token rules point the same way.

Coinbase is also converting any outstanding amounts of non-compliant USDT for its European customers around the 30th of October. Meanwhile, the European Banking Authority designated USDC a significant e-money token in mid-October, bringing it under direct supervision.

Therefore, these regulations are also establishing a framework for how exchanges can service European users.

Ethereum stablecoin addresses surpass 300M

The Ethereum [ETH] stablecoin ecosystem has continued expanding, reaching over 300 million holder addresses. However, the fact that there are over 300 million holder addresses does not automatically mean that there are as many unique and active users.

Approximately three-quarters of these holders reside on layer two networks. This highlights the role that Layer 2 networks have played in increasing access to stablecoins.

When asked if stablecoin gains on Layer 2s translate to real adoption or just balances that flow back to L1, Kovalchuk noted,

Some of both. Part of L2 volume is still trading balances moving back to exchanges. The growth to watch is repeat use: payouts, merchant settlement, and payroll. Once the same businesses settle on L2 every week, that L2 has become a payment rail.

Lower fees associated with layer two networks make it cheaper for individuals to transfer funds using stablecoins. Increased levels of network usage may indicate that individuals are more likely to utilize the same stablecoin multiple times.

But if a few regulated issuers hold most of the market, who carries the risk when one fails? According to Julia,

Holders carry the risk, which is why MiCA’s reserve and redemption rules matter. Europe has moved from one dominant stablecoin to another, so concentration is worth watching. Businesses should ask their platform how many stablecoins it supports and how quickly it can switch if one is restricted.

Together, these trends could shape future competition between USDC and USDT. Ultimately, lasting leadership will depend on regulatory access, deep liquidity, and sustained user activity.

Final Summary
